section: Red flags: 2023 seizure of a Roman bronze bust looted from Turkey
problems: heading states looting as fact; sources report an investigation and the museum's 'likely stolen'
before: Red flags: 2023 seizure of a Roman bronze bust looted from Turkey
after: Red flags: 2023 seizure of a Roman bronze bust in a Turkish looting investigation
reason: WBUR/AP describe a seizure in an ongoing investigation into objects looted from Bubon; no ruling on this bust. The seizure is a documented act, so it stays under Red flags with a heading that names the investigation. All other points confirmed, including the 2025 Italy agreement (The Art Newspaper, Daniel Grant).

problems: repetition: the record's overview already states that about 300 works went to the Louvre in 1962
before: - In 1962 Christian Fouchet, the French Republic's high commissioner in Algeria, decided to transfer works held by the museum to France: 304 works (112 old drawings, 84 modern drawings, 156 paintings) were received and stored in the reserves of the Louvre in May 1962 (Académie des sciences d'outre-mer, ...).
after: - The 1962 transfer of the museum's works to the Louvre was decided by Christian Fouchet, the French Republic's high commissioner in Algeria (Académie des sciences d'outre-mer, Stéphane Richemond, review of ... Abd-el-Tif, 2017).
reason: Kept only what the record lacks (who decided). The review's own breakdown (112+84+156) does not add up to its 304, another reason not to repeat the count. The 1970 restitution dispute and the legal-status point are confirmed word for word.

problems: not a dispute: Gantner's gift conditions
repetition: record funding already names the Gantner gift
repetition: record overview gives the $50 million cost
before: - The new building was first estimated at A$30m and finished at about A$50m, ... - The collector Carrillo Gantner gave more than 350 Aboriginal artworks on two conditions, a standalone gallery and a not-for-profit company independent of the council, saying councils are "not natural operators of major arts facilities" (The Art Newspaper).
after: - Initial estimates put the new building at A$30m against a final figure of about A$50m, ... (Gantner point removed)
reason: The Art Newspaper (Tim Stone, 7 January 2022) confirms the cost rise, the funding shares, Fern Summer's quotes and re-election, and Coates's remark. The point is now the A$30m estimate, since the record already gives the A$50m cost. The gift conditions describe no dispute and were cut.
